verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Cold coffee left on the counter, still warm inside my hands—
someone's name I almost remember.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A ladder against the wall, no one climbing—
just the paint cans waiting,
the whole afternoon still white.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's radio through the fence,
a song I only know the chorus of—
already the light is leaving the wire.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Footsteps stop at the corner, unsure which way—
the streetlamp flickers on
before it's asked to.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing, then quits—
the neighbor's window closes
on whatever it was watching.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone leaves a bicycle unlocked all night—
by morning only the dew
has touched it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The vending machine hums its one note
through the empty lot—
nobody thirsty enough to notice.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A cat crosses the same lot, unbothered—
it counts the puddles instead,
choosing none to drink from.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone finally taps the window—
too late, the bark
already forgiven itself.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain starts without asking permission—
the umbrella stand by the door
stays empty all day.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A phone rings twice in an empty office—
someone's forgotten
what they meant to say.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off on its own—
steam finds the window first,
writes nothing anyone can read.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A dog barks once at the mail truck—
then forgets why,
lies back down in the sun.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns through breakfast—
someone's still asleep
who used to wake us both.
motifs: a sleeper who once woke others

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A grocery list found in a coat pocket—
milk, eggs, call mom,
none of it done yet.
